text:
Zach Hyman spent most of the season's first month on injured reserve, and the Oilers activated him on Nov. 7 along with Devon Levi. In three games back he has three points, including two goals in the win over the Flyers on Nov. 11. With Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Hyman both back, Edmonton is close to the lineup it planned for.

Nine games is too few to judge much. His three goals match his 3.3 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and the Oilers have had 51.3% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice. His team has scored 3.3 more goals than its chances deserved while he's out there, which won't last.

What matters is the job he does. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play in the 98th percentile among forwards last season, with the caveat that he skates with strong teammates, which flatters raw numbers. He's 34, and his game is built on getting to the net. Watch whether his minutes climb back toward 20 a night, which would tell you the Oilers trust his health.
headline: Hyman is healthy again
